Here are **specific, named tutorials and track walk-throughs** that deal with hypnotic/minimal techno top layers and atmospheric percussion, grouped by source and **clearly tied to concrete techniques** (909 toms/congas, resonant filter pings, delay feedback, etc.). I only list items that are explicitly identifiable in the search results and do not invent titles.

## Attack Magazine

### 1. **“Minimal Techno Sound Design Using Soundtoys” – Attack Magazine**[1]

- **URL:** `https://www.attackmagazine.com/technique/tutorials/minimal-techno-sound-design-using-soundtoys`[1]
- **Focus / Technique:**
  - Uses Soundtoys plugins to design **minimal techno percussion and atmospheres**, with emphasis on **short, controlled reverbs and filtering** for top-layer percussion.[1]
  - Shows how to set **very short decay times** (e.g. 0.5 s) and **high low-cut values (around 140 Hz)** on plate reverbs to keep percussion *tight but airy*, so reverb doesn’t interfere with the low end.[1]
  - Demonstrates subtle modulation on reverb (MOD enabled) for evolving tails at longer decay times, which is directly useful for **hypnotic, evolving percussive top layers** in the Plastikman/Dozzy sense.[1]
- **Technique mapping:**
  - **Atmospheric percussion via reverb shaping** (short decays + high-pass/low-cut).
  - **Delay/reverb feedback style ambience** (using Soundtoys EMT140 plate emulation with MOD for smooth evolving tails).[1]

---

### 2. **“Spastik-Style Percussive Techno” – Attack Magazine (Beat Dissected)**[4]

- **URL:** `https://www.attackmagazine.com/technique/beat-dissected/spastik-style-percussive-techno`[4]
- **Focus / Technique:**
  - Explicitly models **Richie Hawtin/Plastikman “Spastik”-style** drum programming.[4]
  - Builds a dense **909-style percussive grid** inside Ableton’s Drum Rack, starting from a Drum Machines “Kick-808” and processing hats and snares for a rolling, hypnotic feel.[4]
  - Uses **909 closed hi-hats** with:
    - Velocity variation via Ableton’s **Velocity MIDI device** (Random for subtle dynamics).[4]
    - High-pass EQ (cutting lows up to around 1.8 kHz) to keep them purely in the high/top layer region.[4]
    - Hard panning to one side (e.g. **50R**) for stereo movement in the percussive layer.[4]
  - Creates **layered snares** (different textures across bars) and additional percussive hits placed at specific points (end of bar, later bars) to anchor the hypnotic rolling feel.[4]
- **Technique mapping:**
  - **909-derived percussive grids** (closed hats, snares, rimshots) with micro-variation.
  - **Top-layer atmospheric movement** via velocity randomization and extreme panning.
  - This is strongly relevant to Plastikman-style **machine-gun 909 tom/hat lattices**, even though the tutorial is framed around kicks/hats rather than explicit tom “pings”.[4]

---

### 3. **“Thumping Techno” – Attack Magazine (Beat Dissected)**[5]

- **URL:** `https://www.attackmagazine.com/technique/beat-dissected/thumping-techno`[5]
- **Focus / Technique:**
  - Uses **analogue drum samples** processed with **filters and saturation** to create a tough techno beat.[5]
  - Adds an **808 tom** and processes it with:
    - A **large but short reverb** for a dense yet controlled impact.[5]
    - **Bitcrushing (D16 Decimort) after the reverb** so the ambience tail is also degraded/colored.[5]
  - Creates **tuned percussion** from a TR-909-style rimshot:
    - Duplicates the rimshot, tunes one low and one high to fit the key of the track.[5]
    - Applies heavy overdrive and a **24 dB/oct high-pass filter**, turning the rim shot into a **pitched, high-frequency percussive “ping”**.[5]
  - Adds a 909 ride, processed with plate reverb and high-pass filtering so it sits as a **bright top-layer pattern** echoing the kick.[5]
- **Technique mapping:**
  - **Filtered 808/909 toms with short reverb** for mid/upper-layer impacts.[5]
  - **Tuned 909 rimshots** as pitched percussive hits via saturation and high-pass filtering (close in spirit to **resonant percussive pings**).[5]
  - **Top-layer rides** treated with reverb and HPF for atmospheric high-end texture.[5]

### 4. **“Sub-Zero Minimal Techno” – Attack Magazine (Beat Dissected)**[2]

- **URL:** `https://www.attackmagazine.com/technique/beat-dissected/sub-zero-minimal-techno`[2]
- **Focus / Technique:**
  - Step-by-step creation of a **minimal techno groove** including subtle percussive top layers.[2]
  - Uses:
    - A snappy rimshot-type percussive hit with **tight envelopes** and optional **automated attack/decay** for variation.[2]
    - A **“subtle halo of reverb”** on that hit to bring it to life without overwhelming the mix.[2]
    - Additional small elements (breathy vocal stab, reversed cymbal) low in the mix to keep the hypnotic feel evolving.[2]
- **Technique mapping:**
  - **Envelope-driven percussive hits** with light ambience for top-layer movement.
  - **Micro-variation in decay/attack** for evolving minimal patterns.
  - **Reverse cymbal and small stabs** as atmospheric ear candy tucked into the top layer.[2]

---

### 5. **“Minimal House” – Attack Magazine (Beat Dissected)**[11]

- **URL:** `https://www.attackmagazine.com/technique/beat-dissected/minimal-house`[11]
- **Focus / Technique:**
  - Although labeled minimal house, the workflow is very applicable to minimal techno top-layer handling.[11]
  - Uses several **glitchy one-shot percussive hits** with quick transients and short decay to add character to the beat.[11]
  - Groups percussion and applies **EQ to remove low end**, plus **tape-style saturation (FabFilter Saturn)** to glue and add grit.[11]
- **Technique mapping:**
  - **Short-decay glitch percussion** as atmospheric top layers.
  - **Grouped processing (HPF + saturation)** to create a cohesive, grainy “cloud” of upper percussion akin to the Dozzy/Mulero/Rødhåd aesthetic.[11]

## Sound On Sound

### 6. **“Classic Tracks: Plastikman ‘Consumed’” – Sound On Sound**[3]

- **URL:** `https://www.soundonsound.com/techniques/classic-tracks-plastikman-consumed`[3]
- **Focus / Technique:**
  - An in-depth production article on **Richie Hawtin’s Plastikman album “Consumed”**.[3]
  - Describes how Hawtin chained **multiple synths and drum machines**, driven by an Atari ST, and **live-manipulated and effected their sounds**, capturing long improvisations to DAT that were later edited.[3]
  - Emphasizes that **everything was recorded as live jams to 2‑track DAT**, with Hawtin constantly searching for a “hook”.[3]
- **Technique mapping (inferred from description + typical Plastikman methods):**
  - While this article is **not a step-by-step sound design tutorial**, it clearly documents:
    - **Live tweaking of filters and effects on drum-machine sequences** (classic environment for **resonant filter pings and hypnotic minimal percussion**).[3]
    - **Improvisation-based creation of evolving percussive textures**, then editing to highlight the most hypnotic sections.[3]
  - Relevant for understanding the **workflow behind Plastikman’s resonant 909-style percussive loops**, but does *not* explicitly specify “filtered 909 toms” or “FM percussion” in a recipe-like manner.[3]

### 10. **“A deep dive with the Erica Synths Graphic Resonant Filterbank!” – YouTube**[9]

- **URL:** `https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=8nS5cuuSKS4`[9]
- **Video title:** **“A deep dive with the Erica Synths Graphic Resonant Filterbank!”**[9]
- **Channel name:** Not visible in the snippet; you’d get it from YouTube directly.
- **Focus / Technique:**
  - Demonstrates the **Erica Synths Graphic Resonant Filterbank**, a multi-band resonant filter module.[9]
  - The snippet specifically notes:
    - It can **self‑oscillate for complex drones**.
    - You can **ping it with pulses to create organic‑sounding percussion**.[9]
- **Technique mapping:**
  - **Resonant filter pings** driven by short pulses to create **organic percussive hits**.[9]
  - Perfectly aligned with the **“filter ping percussion”** aesthetic used in deep/hypnotic techno (Donato Dozzy, Function, etc.).
  - While this is demonstrated on a modular filterbank rather than a standard 909, the **concept maps directly** to any **self‑resonant filter** (e.g., high-resonance LP/BP used as a percussion source).[9]

- **URL:** `https://eprints.hud.ac.uk/id/eprint/18067/1/nbougaiefffinalthesis.pdf`[13]
- **Focus / Technique:**
  - Academic thesis containing discussion of how **Plastikman albums were created** via **long improvised recordings** that were later edited into songs.[13]
  - Describes an improvisation-based production method adapted for stage performance.[13]
- **Technique mapping (contextual):**
  - Supports the notion that **hypnotic Plastikman percussion layers** are the result of **long-form improvisation on drum machines/synths with real-time filter and effect manipulation**, followed by **careful editing**.[13]
  - Not a practical “do X with a 909 tom” tutorial, but very relevant to understanding the **workflow behind these textures**.

## Summary of Techniques Covered Across These Sources

While not all sources explicitly say “Plastikman / Dozzy / Mulero / Rødhåd / Function” in the title, the **techniques** overlap strongly with their aesthetic:

- **Filtered 808/909 toms & tuned rimshots**
  - Attack’s **“Thumping Techno”** shows 808 toms with short reverb and bitcrushing, plus tuned 909 rimshots processed with heavy overdrive and high-pass filtering.[5]
- **Resonant filter pings**
  - YouTube’s **“Resonant filters in techno (+ Reason track walkthrough)”** focuses on resonant filters in a techno context.[8]
  - **Erica Synths Graphic Resonant Filterbank** demo shows self‑oscillation and filter ping percussion.[9]
  - **Octatrack Filter Ping Percussion** video (via Elektronauts) is a dedicated tutorial on creating percussive tones from pinged resonant filters.[14]
- **Atmospheric top-layer percussion via reverb/delay**
  - **“Minimal Techno Sound Design Using Soundtoys”** demonstrates short, high‑passed plate reverbs with modulation for evolving but controlled percussion ambience.[1]
  - Several Beat Dissected articles add **subtle halos of reverb** and **reversed cymbals** as atmospheric top layers in minimal arrangements.[2][5]
- **Hypnotic minimal grid programming**
  - **“Spastik-Style Percussive Techno”** explicitly emulates Hawtin and walks through dense 909-derived percussive grids, velocity randomization, stereo placement, and evolving snare textures.[4]
  - Ableton’s techno tutorial collection focuses on **MIDI‑based techno drum patterns and fills**, useful for building hypnotic repetitive frameworks.[10][15]
